articles.title: Jerry Koosman Dies at 83, World Series Champion Won 222 Games as Pitcher Across 19 MLB Seasons
articles.summary: Former MLB starting pitcher Jerry Koosman, who spent the majority of his career with the New York Mets, has died at the age of 83.
articles.body:
Former MLB starting pitcher Jerry Koosman, who spent the majority of his career with the New York Mets, has died at the age of 83.

"We are saddened to share the news that Jerry Koosman has passed away," the Mets announced Sunday. "We send our thoughts and prayers to his family."

Koosman played for the Mets, Minnesota Twins, Chicago White Sox and Philadelphia Phillies across his 19-year MLB career from 1967-85.

He earned two All-Star nods and won a World Series title with New York in 1969.

Koosman compiled a record of 222-209 across 612 total appearances throughout his career, including 527 starts. 140 of his wins came as a member of the Mets, ranking No. 3 on their all-time leaderboard .

Koosman spent his first 12 seasons in New York, quickly developing into a key piece of the team's rotation.

In the 1969 World Series, the Mets won both of his starts against the Baltimore Orioles. This included a complete game in Game 5 of the series, as New York secured a 5-3 win to capture the franchise's first championship.

The left-hander owned a 3.09 ERA during his Mets tenure before he was eventually traded to the Twins in exchange for relief pitcher Jesse Orosco in 1978.

Koosman spent just over two seasons in Minnesota, finishing with a 39-35 record across 83 starts. He was later dealt to the White Sox in the middle of his 1981 campaign.

Koosman would go on to play for Chicago over the next two years before spending his final pair of MLB seasons in Philadelphia, finally retiring from pitching at the age of 42 years old.

Through his 19 years in the majors, he tallied 2,556 strikeouts compared to 1,198 walks while recording 140 complete games. He also boasted a 3.36 ERA.

Koosman was inducted into the New York Mets Hall of Fame in 1989 before his No. 36 was retired by the club in Aug. 2021.

articles.title: MLB Gold Glove Awards 2026 Full List of Winners and Reaction
articles.summary: The best defensive players in MLB were honored on Sunday.
articles.body:
The best defensive players in MLB were honored on Sunday.

With the season officially coming to a close last week, the 2026 Gold Glove Awards were handed out. Here's a look at this year's winners.

SS: Geraldo Perdomo, Arizona Diamondbacks

RF: Corbin Carroll, Arizona Diamondbacks

Gabriel Moreno winning a Gold Glove makes him the second catcher ever to win a Gold Glove and a batting title in the same season. He joins Minnesota Twins legend Joe Mauer, who achieved the feat in 2008 and 2009.

Moreno slashed .311/.388/.486 with 16 home runs and 83 RBI this year.

With teammates Corbin Carroll and Geraldo Perdomo joining him as Gold Glove winners, the trio became the third group of Diamondbacks players to win the award in the same year.

Dillon Dingler took home his second consecutive Gold Glove, making him the fourth Detroit Tigers player to win the award multiple times and the first since Iván Rodríguez in 2007.

Alex Bregman, who won his second Gold Glove Award, is just the second Cubs third baseman to have won the award, joining Hall of Famer Ron Santo. His teammate, Pete Crow-Armstrong, won his second consecutive Gold Glove.

Mauricio Dubón is in a league of his own when it comes to utility players winning Gold Gloves. He's already won it three times since it was first awarded to utility players in 2022.

For Brice Turang and Jackson Chourio, taking home Gold Glove Awards makes their season even sweeter. Those two helped lead the Brewers to their first World Series title in franchise history, beating the Tampa Bay Rays in five games.
